title: Designing for human–AI complementarity in K-12 education
venue: Proceedings of the ACM Conference on Human Factors in Computing Systems (CHI)
extended_summary:
This paper examines how to design effective human–AI partnerships in K-12 education, focusing on the challenge of helping teachers work productively with AI tutoring systems during live instruction. The authors argue that many human–AI systems fail because they are not designed around real classroom practices, local context, or the complementary strengths of teachers and AI. To address this, they frame the problem as one of augmenting teachers’ situational awareness and decision-making, rather than replacing teacher judgment.

The intervention studied is Lumilo, a pair of mixed-reality smart glasses that give teachers real-time classroom analytics drawn from an AI tutor, including indicators of students’ learning, metacognition, and behavior. The design process was participatory and iterative: teachers with prior experience using AI tutors contributed through field observations, storytelling, card sorting, speed-dating exercises, co-design sessions, replay enactments, and pilot studies. The system was refined using Causal Alignment Analysis, which linked intended student outcomes to teacher behaviors and tool features, and it was piloted in authentic classrooms before a larger field evaluation.

The main field study involved 343 middle school students across 18 classrooms, 8 teachers, and 4 schools and school districts in AI-supported math classes using the Lynnette tutor. Classrooms were randomly assigned to business-as-usual, a glasses-only monitoring condition, or glasses plus analytics. Results showed that Lumilo improved student learning and shifted teacher attention toward students who needed help most, especially lower-performing students. The paper concludes that real-time teacher-facing AI support can improve outcomes when it is designed through deep stakeholder involvement, tested in authentic settings, and explicitly oriented toward complementarity between human judgment and algorithmic analytics.

identified_tools.name: Lumilo
identified_tools.description: A mixed-reality teacher awareness tool implemented with Microsoft HoloLens that overlays real-time analytics, alerts, and student-specific detail screens above students during AI-supported classroom instruction.
identified_tools.use_case: Used by teachers in K-12 classrooms to monitor students working with the AI tutor Lynnette and to support teacher decisions about whom to help and when during live instruction.

findings.finding_summary: In a field experiment with 343 middle school students across 18 classrooms, 8 teachers, and 4 schools/districts, the Glasses + Analytics condition using Lumilo produced higher student learning gains than both business-as-usual and the Glasses-only control. The authors report that Lumilo also reduced the usual 'rich get richer' pattern by shifting teacher attention toward students with lower initial knowledge.
findings.measure: Pre/post learning gains on linear equation solving; teacher attention allocation across students by incoming knowledge
findings.sample_size: n=286 analyzed students (343 enrolled; 57 excluded for absence)

quality_tier_rationale: This is a real-world field experiment in K-12 classrooms with random assignment of classrooms to conditions, but the paper excerpt does not report effect sizes or confidence intervals. The evidence is stronger than qualitative work, yet some methodological detail and full statistical reporting are not present here.
impact_tier_rationale: The paper reports positive learning and attention-allocation effects, but no effect size is provided in the excerpt, so the magnitude cannot be verified. Given the likely educational relevance but incomplete quantitative reporting, the impact is best treated as modest or unclear.
